title: Production Operations, Velero Disaster Recovery & Cluster Maintenance
summary: Master enterprise Kubernetes production operations: declarative disaster recovery and snapshot backups with Velero, restoring persistent state across namespaces, managing zero-downtime worker node maintenance (cordon, drain, uncordon), and validating cluster health with velero CLI.
learningObjectives: Configure automated disaster recovery and namespace snapshots using Velero backup and restore workflows.
Execute safe zero-downtime worker node maintenance using kubectl cordon, drain, and uncordon commands.
Verify backup integrity, storage locations, and restore phases using velero backup and velero restore CLIs.

curriculumModules.title: Disaster Recovery & Backup Automation with Velero
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Velero protects Kubernetes applications and persistent volumes by streaming cluster metadata (etcd resources) and CSI volume snapshots to external object storage (S3, GCS, MinIO). Scheduled backups (e.g. daily-production) combined with point-in-time restores enable instant cross-cluster migration and ransomware disaster recovery.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Enforce daily automated Velero backups with a 30-day retention period, pairing metadata backups with CSI volume snapshots to achieve RPO < 24 hours and RTO < 1 hour.

curriculumModules.title: Node Maintenance Lifecycles: Cordon, Drain & Uncordon
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Routine cluster maintenance (kernel upgrades, AMI cycling, security patching) requires evacuating pods without dropping customer connections. 'kubectl cordon' marks the node Unschedulable. 'kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets' safely evicts workloads while respecting PodDisruptionBudgets. Once updated, 'kubectl uncordon' restores the node to the active scheduler pool.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Automate rolling node drains with maxUnavailable: 1 PDBs to ensure continuous zero-downtime workload availability throughout OS security patch cycles.

labs.title: Creating Automated Velero Backups and Restoring Workloads
labs.scenario: Execute enterprise disaster recovery: create a Velero backup named prod-backup targeting namespace production via velero backup create prod-backup, verify its status with velero backup get, and execute a test restore via velero restore create --from-backup prod-backup.
labs.productionContext: Practicing end-to-end backup and restore operations ensures that platform teams can recover critical revenue-generating state in minutes during data center outages.
objectives: Execute velero backup get to verify status.
Create Velero restore from backup prod-backup.
labs.starterManifest:
# Velero Disaster Recovery Automation
# Run: velero backup create prod-backup && velero restore create --from-backup prod-backup

steps.title: Verify backup creation
steps.instruction: Execute velero backup get to verify status.

troubleshootingGuide.problem: velero command not found or backup failed.
troubleshootingGuide.cause: Commands were not executed or backup name differed from prod-backup.
troubleshootingGuide.solution: Execute velero backup create prod-backup followed by velero restore create --from-backup prod-backup.

labs.title: Zero-Downtime Worker Node Maintenance: Cordon, Drain & Uncordon
labs.scenario: Perform safe kernel maintenance on worker node kubelabs-worker-01: cordon the node to prevent new pod scheduling, drain the node using kubectl drain kubelabs-worker-01 --ignore-daemonsets, simulate the OS upgrade, and uncordon the node to return it to the active pool.
labs.productionContext: Disciplined cordon and drain procedures prevent packet drop and eviction failures during automated cloud instance replacement.

troubleshootingGuide.problem: kubectl drain failed or node remained unschedulable.
troubleshootingGuide.cause: Drain requires --ignore-daemonsets flag to bypass system daemonset pods.
troubleshootingGuide.solution: Execute kubectl drain kubelabs-worker-01 --ignore-daemonsets followed by kubectl uncordon kubelabs-worker-01.

assessmentQuestions.question: In Velero architecture, how are persistent volume data and Kubernetes cluster metadata backed up?
options: Velero takes physical hard drive images of every physical node.

Velero queries the Kubernetes API server for declarative resource YAML manifests and streams them to object storage, while delegating storage volume backup to CSI VolumeSnapshot or restic/Kopia file-level backup.
Velero only backs up Docker container layers.
Velero relies exclusively on Git commit history.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Velero captures all Kubernetes metadata (Deployments, Secrets, CRDs) via the apiserver, compresses them into a tarball in object storage, and triggers CSI VolumeSnapshots for attached persistent volumes.

assessmentQuestions.question: What is the difference between 'kubectl cordon' and 'kubectl drain' during worker node maintenance?
options: Cordon deletes the node while drain restarts it.

Cordon only marks the node as Unschedulable (preventing new pods from being placed on it without affecting running pods); Drain cordons the node AND safely evicts all existing non-daemonset pods while respecting PodDisruptionBudgets.
Cordon is for master nodes; Drain is for worker nodes.
Drain cannot be reversed once executed.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: kubectl cordon marks node.spec.unschedulable: true, leaving active pods untouched. kubectl drain cordons the node and initiates eviction of all existing pods so the host can be safely rebooted or replaced.
